title: Mandatory Attendance vs Medical Exception vs Committee Discretionary Waiver
description: Three conflicting standards governing examination eligibility when attendance falls below 75%.
test_queries: What attendance percentage do I need to sit my end-semester exams if I was hospitalized?
Can the Academic Standing Committee waive my attendance requirement to sit exams if I have 60% attendance?
Can any exception be granted if my attendance is below 75% due to medical reasons?

conflicting_clauses.text: A student must maintain a minimum of 75% attendance across lectures, tutorials, and laboratory practicals in each registered course to be eligible to sit the end-semester examinations. This requirement is strictly mandatory; no exceptions, waivers, or leaves shall be granted under any circumstance, and any student below 75% shall automatically receive an examination debarment notice.

In case of certified medical hospitalization exceeding five (5) consecutive calendar days, the minimum attendance threshold for end-semester examination eligibility shall be lowered to 65%, provided that official medical certificates and discharge summaries are submitted to and endorsed by the University Health Officer within forty-eight (48) hours of discharge.

conflicting_clauses.clause_title: Special Jurisdiction on Examination Attendance Dispensations
conflicting_clauses.text: The Academic Standing & Petitions Committee possesses sole, plenary, and unappealable jurisdiction to grant examination sitting dispensations to any enrolled matriculated student whose course attendance stands between 50.0% and 74.9%, upon formal petition submitted to the Committee at least seven (7) calendar days prior to the commencement of the examination period.

point_of_tension: Clause 4.2(a) explicitly asserts that 75% attendance is strictly mandatory with 'no exceptions under any circumstance'. However, Clause 8.1(c) provides an exception lowering the threshold to 65% for hospitalized illness, and Clause 14.3 of the Disciplinary Charter empowers the Academic Standing Committee with plenary jurisdiction to grant sitting waivers down to 50% upon advance petition.
administrative_ambiguity: A student with 60% attendance who was hospitalized or who petitions the committee receives opposite answers depending on which regulation is read: Debarred with no exception under 4.2(a), ineligible under 8.1(c) (which requires 65%), yet eligible for a plenary waiver under 14.3.

title: Hostel 22:00 Curfew & Lock-Out Fine vs 24-Hour Research Lab Privileges
topic: Residential Curfew vs Overnight Laboratory Access
description: Hostel rules mandate curfew lock-out and fines after 22:00, while Academic Regulations grant 24-hour lab access and forbid hostel lockouts or fines.
test_queries: Will I be locked out or fined if I return to my hostel at 1 AM after working on my capstone project in the lab?
Can hostel security fine me $50 if I return past 10 PM from an authorized overnight lab session?
Does hostel curfew apply to final-year engineering students working overnight in the computer center?

conflicting_clauses.clause_title: Mandatory 22:00 Curfew and Strict Gate Penalties
conflicting_clauses.text: A mandatory residential gate curfew is strictly enforced across all undergraduate hostels at 22:00 (10:00 PM) daily. Any resident entering the residential precinct or dormitory block after 22:00 without a physical, pre-authorized written warden leave slip signed before 17:00 of the same day shall incur a mandatory fine of $50 and shall be locked out of the hostel until 06:00 the following morning. Security wardens have zero discretion to waive this lock-out.

conflicting_clauses.clause_title: Research Facility and 24-Hour Computing Lab Privileges
conflicting_clauses.text: All enrolled final-year capstone students, honors thesis candidates, and authorized engineering research scholars are granted unhindered twenty-four-hour (24-hour) keycard access to designated campus research laboratories, maker spaces, and the central computing center. Campus security officers, night watchmen, and residential hall wardens are expressly prohibited from impeding, questioning, or locking out students returning to their residence halls from authorized overnight laboratory work sessions, and no fines or disciplinary penalties of any kind shall be levied on such students.

point_of_tension: Hostel Clause 3.4 mandates a $50 fine and absolute lock-out until 06:00 for any entry past 22:00 without a pre-approved warden slip signed by 17:00. Conversely, Academic Regulation Clause 11.2(b) grants 24-hour access and expressly prohibits wardens and security from locking out capstone students or levying any fines.
administrative_ambiguity: A final-year student returning to the hostel at 01:00 AM from an authorized lab session is legally protected by Academic Regulations §11.2(b) from lock-out and fines, yet subject to mandatory lock-out and a $50 fine under Hostel Policy §3.4.

title: Course Drop Refund Schedule: Academic Policy 80% vs Fee Table 0% Forfeiture
topic: Tuition Refund for Course Drop in Weeks 3-4
description: Academic Regulations promise an 80% tuition refund up to Day 28, while the Fee Schedule table mandates 0% refund (100% forfeiture) after Day 14.
test_queries: If I drop a course on Day 21 (Week 3), what refund percentage do I get?
Can I get a refund if I withdraw from a class in Week 4 of the semester?
Does the university refund 80% of tuition if I drop a course before Day 28?

conflicting_clauses.text: Any student who officially drops or withdraws from a semester course prior to the conclusion of Week 4 (Day 28 of the semester instruction calendar) through the student academic portal is entitled to an eighty percent (80%) prorated tuition fee refund for the credits associated with that course.

0% Refund (100% Tuition Forfeiture). Strict forfeiture policy. No tuition refunds, rebates, or credits shall be issued for course drops or withdrawals recorded between Day 15 and Day 35 of the academic semester.

point_of_tension: Academic Regulations §6.3 specifies an 80% tuition refund for drops logged prior to Day 28 (Week 4), whereas the Fee Deadlines and Refunds Schedule (Row 4) explicitly states that withdrawals logged between Day 15 and Day 35 receive a 0% refund (100% forfeiture).
administrative_ambiguity: A student dropping a course on Day 21 is entitled to an 80% refund according to Academic Regulations, but will be denied any refund (0%) by the Bursar's Office applying the Fee Schedule table.
